about: DRAFT, never run. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B, NVIDIA's QAD 24 GB GGUF (IQ2_XXS experts, NVFP4 Mamba, Q8_0 embeddings/head) with its image projector and NVIDIA's LiLiCorr GGUF drafter (draft-dflash, 7 tokens), all on the RTX Spark N1X's GPU. NVIDIA's own '32GB recipe for RTX Spark 128GB' from the GGUF card: batch 4096 / ubatch 2048, 262,144 context, one slot, flash attention. Upstream llama.cpp b11718 (547208dc, CUDA 13.4.1, one index digest over linux/amd64 + linux/arm64): Bolt/Super VL support landed in b11658+ (#30520), LiLiCorr drafts in b11641 (#30506), faster MMVQ for low-bit types in b11713 (#30517). --load-mode none as in the N1X flash-next draft. 24.75 GB of weights; the KV is 8 KB a token (8 attention layers x 2 KV heads), so 262,144 tokens is ~2 GiB bf16.

plugin.name: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B
plugin.format: GGUF · NVIDIA 24 GB (IQ2_XXS / NVFP4 / Q8_0) + LiLiCorr

setup: One RTX Spark N1X. ~25 GB of downloads (22.02 GB GGUF + 1.73 GB mmproj + 1.00 GB LiLiCorr GGUF). Expected resident memory ~31 GiB at 262,144 tokens with the drafter (Classmethod measured 31.4 GiB on a DGX Spark with the same flags), so the desktop keeps plenty. Reference speeds, not measured here: DGX Spark llama.cpp 39.5 tok/s without drafts, 61.6 tok/s with the LiLiCorr drafter (dev.classmethod.jp, 2026-10-16); NVIDIA cites ~84 tok/s on RTX Spark. No network at runtime: the drafter is a pinned GGUF mounted at /draft.
